title.rendered: Blessed Are the Persecuted: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake.” A morning devotional for anyone who has paid a cost for following Christ.

content.rendered:
In 155 AD, an elderly bishop named Polycarp of Smyrna was arrested by Roman authorities and given a choice. Renounce Christ or be burned alive. His answer has echoed through eighteen centuries of the persecuted church. “Eighty-six years have I served Him, and He has done me no wrong. How then can I blaspheme my King, who has saved me?”

The Gospel For Today | Friday, September 4, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, For theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are you when they revile and persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely for My sake. Rejoice and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven, for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.”
Matthew 5:10-12 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In the year 155 AD, in the city of Smyrna on the Aegean coast, an elderly bishop named Polycarp was arrested by Roman authorities during a wave of persecution. Polycarp had been a disciple of the apostle John. He was now over eighty years old. He was brought before the Roman proconsul in the stadium of Smyrna and given a choice. Renounce Christ. Curse the name of Jesus. Or be burned alive. Polycarp’s answer has echoed through eighteen centuries of the persecuted church. “Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He has never done me wrong. How then can I blaspheme my King who saved me?” Polycarp was tied to a stake in the stadium and burned that day. His last recorded words were a prayer of thanksgiving.

Jesus knew this kind of testimony would come from the church He was launching. On the hillside in Galilee, as He closed the beatitudes, He named the persecuted. Not as an afterthought. As the culmination. “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are you when they revile and persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely for My sake. Rejoice and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven.”

The Passion Translation captures the paradox of the beatitude: “How enriched you become when you bear the wounds of being persecuted for doing what is right! For that is when you experience the realm of heaven’s kingdom” (Matthew 5:10 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Blessed and happy and enviably fortunate and spiritually prosperous (in the state in which the born-again child of God enjoys and finds satisfaction in God’s favor and salvation, regardless of his outward conditions) are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake (for being and doing right), for theirs is the kingdom of heaven!” (Matthew 5:10 AMPC).

The persecution Jesus names is specifically for righteousness’ sake, for His sake. Not the natural consequence of unwise decisions. Not the friction of ordinary human conflict. The persecution that comes because a believer will not deny Jesus, will not compromise on the gospel, will not bow to a rival lord, will not stop preaching, will not stop living faithfully. That kind of persecution, Jesus says, is the mark of belonging to a Kingdom no earthly regime can shake. The rulers of Rome could take Polycarp’s life. They could not take his citizenship in the Kingdom of heaven.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, the beatitude is not only for the persecuted church in Nigeria, Iran, North Korea, and China, though we honour and pray for those brothers and sisters. It is also for the ordinary believer facing quieter forms of hostility for their faith, in workplaces where the gospel is mocked, in classrooms where Christianity is dismissed, in social settings where following Jesus makes you the odd one out. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if you have known even a shadow of the cost Jesus described, He calls you blessed. The Kingdom is yours. The reward is great. Rejoice.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus called the persecuted blessed. He knew what following Him would cost. I honour today the persecuted brothers and sisters around the world who are paying that cost with their freedom, their families, their bodies, their lives. I pray for them. I stand with them. And whatever cost following Jesus is asking of me in my own quieter setting, I refuse to deny His name. The Kingdom is worth more than the comfort. The reward is greater than the loss. I walk in that today. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Blessed are the persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of heaven. I refuse to deny His name. The Kingdom is worth more than any comfort I might lose. My reward is great.
